top_news.title: Deakin forges landmark partnerships with CII and LinkedIn to advance India
top_news.summary: As part of its commitment to deepening engagement in India and preparing learners for the future of work, Deakin University has established two landmark strategic partnerships with LinkedIn and the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII). Together, these collaborations strengthen the bridge between academia and industry, equipping learners with future-ready skills, valuable professional networks, and real-world opportunities to thrive in a rapidly evolving workforce. The partnerships reflect Deakin's continued commitment to working in India, with India and for India, bringing together education, industry expertise and workforce insights to bridge the gap between academic learning and the changing needs of employers. Deakin and LinkedIn partner to strengthen career readiness and professional skills Earlier this week, Deakin signed a partnership agreement with LinkedIn at its GIFT City campus in Gandhinagar, establishing a platform for collaboration around student employability, professional development and workforce readiness. Ms Saba Karim, India Head-SMB, Public Sector, Education at LinkedIn mentioned, "At LinkedIn, we believe opportunity begins with the right skills and connections. Our partnership with Deakin will help equip students with workforce insights, professional networks, and career-ready capabilities to thrive in the jobs of tomorrow." Key areas of engagement include professional branding and profile development, career readiness, networking, job-search strategies, interview preparation and insights into emerging skills and labour-market trends. The collaboration will also explore opportunities for student and faculty engagement, leadership development and knowledge-sharing on artificial intelligence (AI), evolving job roles and the future of work. Through potential initiatives such as professional development workshops, career-focused sessions, industry interactions and access to workforce insights, the partnership seeks to strengthen the connection between students' academic experiences and their career aspirations. Opportunities for leadership engagement and thought leadership will further support conversations around the skills and capabilities needed in a rapidly changing world of work. The agreement reinforces Deakin's approach to employability as an integral part of the learning experience at the GIFT City Campus, ensuring learning translates into opportunity. Deakin and CII advance the Global Job Readiness Program for India's evolving workforce Building on its focus on industry-aligned education and skills development, Deakin University signed an agreement with the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) at the Australian High Commission in New Delhi today to advance the Global Job Readiness Program (GJRP), its flagship skilling and continuous learning program. A significant milestone in the partnership is the program's approval by the National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET). This enables the program to be integrated into university curricula and support credit recognition in alignment with India's National Education Policy (NEP) skills-development framework, subject to applicable requirements. Mr Sougata Roy Choudhury, Executive Director, CII, welcomed the collaboration, stating, "The Global Job Readiness Program is an important step towards interfacing education and industry expectations. By equipping learners with skills that are relevant to today's employment landscape and aligning the programme with India's national skills framework, we aim to strengthen employability and create pathways for universities to integrate job-readiness learning into formal higher education." Following the successful completion of the first phase of the partnership, CII is taking the program to market, with a focus on institutional outreach, awareness-building and enrolments across universities and higher-education institutions. The program will be delivered 100% online with flexibility, much needed for young learners and professionals, and certification arrangements are aligned with applicable National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) guidelines. Through this model, Deakin and CII aim to expand access to structured job-readiness learning and strengthen the role of industry in preparing graduates for employment. At the same event, CII exchanged LoIs with five Indian institutions to strengthen collaboration, including efforts to expand the reach of the Global Job Readiness Program and extend its benefits to students across their campuses. The participating institutions include Rukmani Devi Institute of Advanced Studies, Gateway Institute of Engineering and Technology, University of Engineering and Management (UEM), Jaipur, AAFT University, and Inderprastha Engineering College. George Thiveos, Minister Counsellor Education and Research, South Asia for the Australian Gov, Dept of Education, welcomed the initiative and said, "Deakin and CII are both institutions that are very well established and at the forefront of their respective fields, and I find them very well matched for this initiative." "The government can play a critical role through policy and create pathways for meaningful B2B collaboration. I see India and Australia contributing meaningfully towards India's goal for Viksit Bharat 2047." Mukund Narayanamurti, Minister (Commercial), General Manager and Head of Austrade South Asia, added, "Deakin has rendered significant contribution to bilateral cooperation and there cannot be a more impactful partner to Deakin than CII. The work of CII and Deakin aligns with a lot of our objectives such as advancing workforce capabilities, graduate readiness with a lens on enhancing employability." Expressing her thoughts on these key initiatives, Ravneet Pawha, Vice President (Global Engagement) and CEO (South Asia), Deakin University, said, "The future of work will be shaped by collaboration. Through our partnerships with LinkedIn and CII, we are creating meaningful pathways that connect learning with opportunity and prepare learners to thrive in a changing world." "I am truly optimistic about the far-reaching impact that can be created through these partnerships and look forward to young students and professionals taking advantage of this." Together, the partnerships with LinkedIn and CII demonstrate Deakin's multi-dimensional approach to future-of-work readiness

The partnerships reflect Deakin's continued commitment to working in India, with India and for India, bringing together education, industry expertise and workforce insights to bridge the gap between academic learning and the changing needs of employers. Deakin and LinkedIn partner to strengthen career readiness and professional skills Earlier this week, Deakin signed a partnership agreement with LinkedIn at its GIFT City campus in Gandhinagar, establishing a platform for collaboration around student employability, professional development and workforce readiness. Ms Saba Karim, India Head-SMB, Public Sector, Education at LinkedIn mentioned, At LinkedIn, we believe opportunity begins with the right skills and connections. Our partnership with Deakin will help equip students with workforce insights, professional networks, and career-ready capabilities to thrive in the jobs of tomorrow. Key areas of engagement include professional branding and profile development, career readiness, networking, job-search strategies, interview preparation and insights into emerging skills and labour-market trends. The collaboration will also explore opportunities for student and faculty engagement, leadership development and knowledge-sharing on artificial intelligence (AI), evolving job roles and the future of work. Through potential initiatives such as professional development workshops, career-focused sessions, industry interactions and access to workforce insights, the partnership seeks to strengthen the connection between students' academic experiences and their career aspirations. Opportunities for leadership engagement and thought leadership will further support conversations around the skills and capabilities needed in a rapidly changing world of work. The agreement reinforces Deakin's approach to employability as an integral part of the learning experience at the GIFT City Campus, ensuring learning translates into opportunity. Deakin and CII advance the Global Job Readiness Program for India's evolving workforce Building on its focus on industry-aligned education and skills development, Deakin University signed an agreement with the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) at the Australian High Commission in New Delhi today to advance the Global Job Readiness Program (GJRP), its flagship skilling and continuous learning program. A significant milestone in the partnership is the program's approval by the National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET). This enables the program to be integrated into university curricula and support credit recognition in alignment with India's National Education Policy (NEP) skills-development framework, subject to applicable requirements. Mr Sougata Roy Choudhury, Executive Director, CII, welcomed the collaboration, stating, The Global Job Readiness Program is an important step towards interfacing education and industry expectations. By equipping learners with skills that are relevant to today's employment landscape and aligning the programme with India's national skills framework, we aim to strengthen employability and create pathways for universities to integrate job-readiness learning into formal higher education. Following the successful completion of the first phase of the partnership, CII is taking the program to market, with a focus on institutional outreach, awareness-building and enrolments across universities and higher-education institutions. The program will be delivered 100% online with flexibility, much needed for young learners and professionals, and certification arrangements are aligned with applicable National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) guidelines. Through this model, Deakin and CII aim to expand access to structured job-readiness learning and strengthen the role of industry in preparing graduates for employment. At the same event, CII exchanged LoIs with five Indian institutions to strengthen collaboration, including efforts to expand the reach of the Global Job Readiness Program and extend its benefits to students across their campuses. The participating institutions include Rukmani Devi Institute of Advanced Studies, Gateway Institute of Engineering and Technology, University of Engineering and Management (UEM), Jaipur, AAFT University, and Inderprastha Engineering College. George Thiveos, Minister Counsellor Education and Research, South Asia for the Australian Gov, Dept of Education, welcomed the initiative and said, Deakin and CII are both institutions that are very well established and at the forefront of their respective fields, and I find them very well matched for this initiative. The government can play a critical role through policy and create pathways for meaningful B2B collaboration. I see India and Australia contributing meaningfully towards India's goal for Viksit Bharat 2047. Mukund Narayanamurti, Minister (Commercial), General Manager and Head of Austrade South Asia, added, Deakin has rendered significant contribution to bilateral cooperation and there cannot be a more impactful partner to Deakin than CII. The work of CII and Deakin aligns with a lot of our objectives such as advancing workforce capabilities, graduate readiness with a lens on enhancing employability. Expressing her thoughts on these key initiatives, Ravneet Pawha, Vice President (Global Engagement) and CEO (South Asia), Deakin University, said, The future of work will be shaped by collaboration. Through our partnerships with LinkedIn and CII, we are creating meaningful pathways that connect learning with opportunity and prepare learners to thrive in a changing world. I am truly optimistic about the far-reaching impact that can be created through these partnerships and look forward to young students and professionals taking advantage of this. Together, the partnerships with LinkedIn and CII demonstrate Deakin's multi-dimensional approach to future-of-work readiness: connecting students with professional networks and workforce insights while advancing structured, industry-aligned skills development through institutional collaboration. As AI, digital technologies and changing workforce expectations reshape employment, collaboration between universities, industry bodies and professional platforms is increasingly important to ensure that education remains relevant to emerging opportunities. Hence, Deakin continues to build connections between education and industry, with a shared focus on helping learners develop the skills, confidence and capabilities to succeed in a dynamic global economy. About Deakin University: Established in 1974, Deakin University successfully combines excellence in teaching, research and effective partnerships with industry and government to deliver high-quality courses and undertake research that makes a difference to the domestic and international communities it serves. Deakin's South Asia operations commenced in 1994 in New Delhi, India, making it one of the first overseas education providers to set up operations in this region. Here, Deakin engages with the government, industry, and academia to share its vibrant culture of education and research. To know more about Deakin University and its various initiatives as part of its 'in India, with India, for India' approach towards engagement, please visit https://www.deakin.edu.au/ About LinkedIn - LinkedIn connects the world's professionals to make them more productive and successful and transforms how companies hire, learn, market, and sell. Our vision is to create economic opportunity for every member of the global workforce through the ongoing development of the world's first Economic Graph. LinkedIn has over 1.3 billion members and has offices around the globe. About CII - CII has been shaping India's development journey for more than 130 years. The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) is an industry-led and industry-managed organisation that works to create and sustain an environment conducive to India's development, partnering industry, Government and civil society. We have around 9,700 direct members and an indirect membership of over 365,000 enterprises through 318 industry bodies, with 70 offices in India, including 12 Centres of Excellence, and 9 overseas offices in Australia, Egypt, Germany, Indonesia, Singapore, UAE, UK and USA. Along with partnerships with 255 counterpart organisations in 102 countries, CII serves as a reference point for Indian industry and the international business community. top_news.title: Nature Conference India 2026 at MAHE Manipal puts infectious disease threats under the scientific spotlight
top_news.summary: VMPL Manipal [India], October 16: As drug-resistant infections spread, climate change reshapes disease patterns and lessons from COVID-19 remain fresh, some of the world's leading infectious disease experts spent three days at the Manipal Academy of Higher Education (MAHE), Manipal, searching for answers. The second Nature Conference in India, 'Meeting the challenge of infectious diseases in a changing world', concluded today. Held from 14 to 16 October and organised by Nature Medicine, Nature Microbiology, Nature Health, Nature Communications and MAHE, the conference brought together researchers and public health experts from India and around the world. Sessions covered disease surveillance and forecasting, antimicrobial resistance (AMR), diagnostics, disease prevention, vaccine development, climate change and pandemic preparedness, with a focus on challenges that matter to India's health system. The conference follows the first Nature Conference in India, also held at MAHE Manipal in 2024 on nanomaterials in biomedical applications. Dr Sharath K. Rao, Vice Chancellor, MAHE said: Hosting the second Nature Conference in India at MAHE is an important opportunity to bring together researchers and experts working across disciplines and geographies. Infectious diseases present complex challenges that require scientific collaboration, sustained research and the exchange of knowledge. We are pleased to partner with Nature Portfolio in creating a platform for meaningful scientific engagement and in supporting conversations that can contribute to the advancement of research and public health. Lorenzo Righetto, Senior Editor, Nature Health, said: Addressing infectious diseases requires a deeper understanding of emerging pathogens, antimicrobial resistance, disease prevention and the wider environmental factors that influence health. The Nature Conference brings together researchers working across these areas, creating opportunities for scientific exchange and interdisciplinary collaboration. We are delighted to continue our partnership with MAHE and support a forum that enables the research community to engage with some of the most pressing challenges in global health. The programme featured keynote addresses, research presentations and poster sessions, bringing together perspectives from epidemiology, microbiology, public health, clinical research and environmental science. Discussions examined the importance of strengthening surveillance systems, improving disease detection, advancing treatment and prevention strategies, and understanding the connections between environmental change and infectious disease risk. Big ideas from the keynotes: * Learning from COVID-19: Lauren Gardner of Johns Hopkins University spoke on public health in the post-COVID era and the role of data in decision-making. * Rethinking TB diagnosis: Madhukar Pai of McGill University addressed how tuberculosis diagnosis can be transformed, a priority for India, which carries a large share of the global TB burden. * Protecting children: Shabir A. Madhi of the University of the Witwatersrand examined progress and challenges in preventing vaccine-preventable respiratory infections in children. * Predicting the next outbreak: Marion Koopmans of Erasmus University Rotterdam discussed outbreak risk prediction as a pillar of preparedness. Other sessions explored antimicrobial resistance and the development of new treatments, including research on Klebsiella pneumoniae and tuberculosis regimens. Discussions on diagnostics and prevention included HPV testing and vaccination, the development of vaccines for emerging and endemic infectious diseases, and approaches to improving access to long-acting preventive interventions. The conference also examined the relationship between climate change and infectious diseases, including changing vector-borne disease risks, childhood malnutrition and antimicrobial resistance through a One Health perspective. These discussions highlighted the relevance of interdisciplinary research in understanding the interconnected factors shaping global health challenges. Research presentations and poster sessions let early-career and established researchers present their work and build connections across institutions and disciplines. The programme concluded with poster awards and closing remarks. By bringing together epidemiologists, microbiologists, clinicians, public health specialists and environmental scientists, the conference underlined that tackling emerging health threats will depend on collaboration across disciplines and geographies. About Nature Nature is a leading international scientific journal, publishing high-quality, peer-reviewed research across a wide range of disciplines. Part of Springer Nature, it is widely recognised for its role in advancing scientific discovery and providing a platform for significant breakthroughs that shape global understanding of science and health. Springer Nature is one of the leading publishers of research in the world, publishing the largest number of journals and books and are a pioneer in open research. Through our leading brands, trusted for more than 180 years, we provide technology-enabled products, platforms and services that help researchers to uncover new ideas and share their discoveries, health professionals to stay at the forefront of medical science, and educators to advance learning. We are proud to be part of progress, working together with the communities we serve to share knowledge and bring greater understanding to the world. For more information, please visit nature.com and follow Nature Portfolio. About Manipal Academy of Higher Education (MAHE) Manipal Academy of Higher Education (MAHE) is an Institution of Eminence Deemed to be University. MAHE offers over 400 specialisations across the Health Sciences (HS), Management, Law, Humanities & Social Sciences (MLHS), and Technology & Science (T&S) streams through its constituent units at campuses in Manipal, Mangalore, Bengaluru, Jamshedpur, and Dubai. With a remarkable track record in academics, state-of-the-art infrastructure, and significant contributions to research, MAHE has earned recognition and acclaim both nationally and internationally. In 2020, the Ministry of Education, Government of India, awarded MAHE the prestigious Institution of Eminence status. Currently ranked 3rd in the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) 2025 rankings, MAHE is the preferred choice for students seeking a transformative learning experience and enriching campus life, as well as for national and multinational corporations seeking top talent. articles.summary: Deep down, we know that if something goes catastrophically wrong six miles in the air, almost nothing can save us. Except pure chance. That is exactly what saved 22-year-old Serbian flight attendant Vesna Vulović when her plane exploded mid-air in 1972. Trapped inside the wreckage, she fell 33,000 feet onto the snowy slopes of Czechoslovakia. Out of 28 people on board, she was the lone survivor. Read on for her remarkable story of survival against all human odds.

articles.title: Deakin forges landmark partnerships with CII and LinkedIn to advance India
articles.summary: As part of its commitment to deepening engagement in India and preparing learners for the future of work, Deakin University has established two landmark strategic partnerships with LinkedIn and the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII). Together, these collaborations strengthen the bridge between academia and industry, equipping learners with future-ready skills, valuable professional networks, and real-world opportunities to thrive in a rapidly evolving workforce. The partnerships reflect Deakin's continued commitment to working in India, with India and for India, bringing together education, industry expertise and workforce insights to bridge the gap between academic learning and the changing needs of employers. Deakin and LinkedIn partner to strengthen career readiness and professional skills Earlier this week, Deakin signed a partnership agreement with LinkedIn at its GIFT City campus in Gandhinagar, establishing a platform for collaboration around student employability, professional development and workforce readiness. Ms Saba Karim, India Head-SMB, Public Sector, Education at LinkedIn mentioned, "At LinkedIn, we believe opportunity begins with the right skills and connections. Our partnership with Deakin will help equip students with workforce insights, professional networks, and career-ready capabilities to thrive in the jobs of tomorrow." Key areas of engagement include professional branding and profile development, career readiness, networking, job-search strategies, interview preparation and insights into emerging skills and labour-market trends. The collaboration will also explore opportunities for student and faculty engagement, leadership development and knowledge-sharing on artificial intelligence (AI), evolving job roles and the future of work. Through potential initiatives such as professional development workshops, career-focused sessions, industry interactions and access to workforce insights, the partnership seeks to strengthen the connection between students' academic experiences and their career aspirations. Opportunities for leadership engagement and thought leadership will further support conversations around the skills and capabilities needed in a rapidly changing world of work. The agreement reinforces Deakin's approach to employability as an integral part of the learning experience at the GIFT City Campus, ensuring learning translates into opportunity. Deakin and CII advance the Global Job Readiness Program for India's evolving workforce Building on its focus on industry-aligned education and skills development, Deakin University signed an agreement with the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) at the Australian High Commission in New Delhi today to advance the Global Job Readiness Program (GJRP), its flagship skilling and continuous learning program. A significant milestone in the partnership is the program's approval by the National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET). This enables the program to be integrated into university curricula and support credit recognition in alignment with India's National Education Policy (NEP) skills-development framework, subject to applicable requirements. Mr Sougata Roy Choudhury, Executive Director, CII, welcomed the collaboration, stating, "The Global Job Readiness Program is an important step towards interfacing education and industry expectations. By equipping learners with skills that are relevant to today's employment landscape and aligning the programme with India's national skills framework, we aim to strengthen employability and create pathways for universities to integrate job-readiness learning into formal higher education." Following the successful completion of the first phase of the partnership, CII is taking the program to market, with a focus on institutional outreach, awareness-building and enrolments across universities and higher-education institutions. The program will be delivered 100% online with flexibility, much needed for young learners and professionals, and certification arrangements are aligned with applicable National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) guidelines. Through this model, Deakin and CII aim to expand access to structured job-readiness learning and strengthen the role of industry in preparing graduates for employment. At the same event, CII exchanged LoIs with five Indian institutions to strengthen collaboration, including efforts to expand the reach of the Global Job Readiness Program and extend its benefits to students across their campuses. The participating institutions include Rukmani Devi Institute of Advanced Studies, Gateway Institute of Engineering and Technology, University of Engineering and Management (UEM), Jaipur, AAFT University, and Inderprastha Engineering College. George Thiveos, Minister Counsellor Education and Research, South Asia for the Australian Gov, Dept of Education, welcomed the initiative and said, "Deakin and CII are both institutions that are very well established and at the forefront of their respective fields, and I find them very well matched for this initiative." "The government can play a critical role through policy and create pathways for meaningful B2B collaboration. I see India and Australia contributing meaningfully towards India's goal for Viksit Bharat 2047." Mukund Narayanamurti, Minister (Commercial), General Manager and Head of Austrade South Asia, added, "Deakin has rendered significant contribution to bilateral cooperation and there cannot be a more impactful partner to Deakin than CII. The work of CII and Deakin aligns with a lot of our objectives such as advancing workforce capabilities, graduate readiness with a lens on enhancing employability." Expressing her thoughts on these key initiatives, Ravneet Pawha, Vice President (Global Engagement) and CEO (South Asia), Deakin University, said, "The future of work will be shaped by collaboration. Through our partnerships with LinkedIn and CII, we are creating meaningful pathways that connect learning with opportunity and prepare learners to thrive in a changing world." "I am truly optimistic about the far-reaching impact that can be created through these partnerships and look forward to young students and professionals taking advantage of this." Together, the partnerships with LinkedIn and CII demonstrate Deakin's multi-dimensional approach to future-of-work readiness

We have around 9,700 direct members and an indirect membership of over 365,000 enterprises through 318 industry bodies, with 70 offices in India, including 12 Centres of Excellence, and 9 overseas offices in Australia, Egypt, Germany, Indonesia, Singapore, UAE, UK and USA. articles.title: Nature Conference India 2026 at MAHE Manipal puts infectious disease threats under the scientific spotlight
articles.summary: VMPL Manipal [India], October 16: As drug-resistant infections spread, climate change reshapes disease patterns and lessons from COVID-19 remain fresh, some of the world's leading infectious disease experts spent three days at the Manipal Academy of Higher Education (MAHE), Manipal, searching for answers. The second Nature Conference in India, 'Meeting the challenge of infectious diseases in a changing world', concluded today. Held from 14 to 16 October and organised by Nature Medicine, Nature Microbiology, Nature Health, Nature Communications and MAHE, the conference brought together researchers and public health experts from India and around the world. Sessions covered disease surveillance and forecasting, antimicrobial resistance (AMR), diagnostics, disease prevention, vaccine development, climate change and pandemic preparedness, with a focus on challenges that matter to India's health system. The conference follows the first Nature Conference in India, also held at MAHE Manipal in 2024 on nanomaterials in biomedical applications. Dr Sharath K. Rao, Vice Chancellor, MAHE said: Hosting the second Nature Conference in India at MAHE is an important opportunity to bring together researchers and experts working across disciplines and geographies. Infectious diseases present complex challenges that require scientific collaboration, sustained research and the exchange of knowledge. We are pleased to partner with Nature Portfolio in creating a platform for meaningful scientific engagement and in supporting conversations that can contribute to the advancement of research and public health. Lorenzo Righetto, Senior Editor, Nature Health, said: Addressing infectious diseases requires a deeper understanding of emerging pathogens, antimicrobial resistance, disease prevention and the wider environmental factors that influence health. The Nature Conference brings together researchers working across these areas, creating opportunities for scientific exchange and interdisciplinary collaboration. We are delighted to continue our partnership with MAHE and support a forum that enables the research community to engage with some of the most pressing challenges in global health. The programme featured keynote addresses, research presentations and poster sessions, bringing together perspectives from epidemiology, microbiology, public health, clinical research and environmental science. Discussions examined the importance of strengthening surveillance systems, improving disease detection, advancing treatment and prevention strategies, and understanding the connections between environmental change and infectious disease risk. Big ideas from the keynotes: * Learning from COVID-19: Lauren Gardner of Johns Hopkins University spoke on public health in the post-COVID era and the role of data in decision-making. * Rethinking TB diagnosis: Madhukar Pai of McGill University addressed how tuberculosis diagnosis can be transformed, a priority for India, which carries a large share of the global TB burden. * Protecting children: Shabir A. Madhi of the University of the Witwatersrand examined progress and challenges in preventing vaccine-preventable respiratory infections in children. * Predicting the next outbreak: Marion Koopmans of Erasmus University Rotterdam discussed outbreak risk prediction as a pillar of preparedness. Other sessions explored antimicrobial resistance and the development of new treatments, including research on Klebsiella pneumoniae and tuberculosis regimens. Discussions on diagnostics and prevention included HPV testing and vaccination, the development of vaccines for emerging and endemic infectious diseases, and approaches to improving access to long-acting preventive interventions. The conference also examined the relationship between climate change and infectious diseases, including changing vector-borne disease risks, childhood malnutrition and antimicrobial resistance through a One Health perspective. These discussions highlighted the relevance of interdisciplinary research in understanding the interconnected factors shaping global health challenges. Research presentations and poster sessions let early-career and established researchers present their work and build connections across institutions and disciplines. The programme concluded with poster awards and closing remarks. By bringing together epidemiologists, microbiologists, clinicians, public health specialists and environmental scientists, the conference underlined that tackling emerging health threats will depend on collaboration across disciplines and geographies. About Nature Nature is a leading international scientific journal, publishing high-quality, peer-reviewed research across a wide range of disciplines. Part of Springer Nature, it is widely recognised for its role in advancing scientific discovery and providing a platform for significant breakthroughs that shape global understanding of science and health. Springer Nature is one of the leading publishers of research in the world, publishing the largest number of journals and books and are a pioneer in open research. Through our leading brands, trusted for more than 180 years, we provide technology-enabled products, platforms and services that help researchers to uncover new ideas and share their discoveries, health professionals to stay at the forefront of medical science, and educators to advance learning. We are proud to be part of progress, working together with the communities we serve to share knowledge and bring greater understanding to the world. For more information, please visit nature.com and follow Nature Portfolio. About Manipal Academy of Higher Education (MAHE) Manipal Academy of Higher Education (MAHE) is an Institution of Eminence Deemed to be University. MAHE offers over 400 specialisations across the Health Sciences (HS), Management, Law, Humanities & Social Sciences (MLHS), and Technology & Science (T&S) streams through its constituent units at campuses in Manipal, Mangalore, Bengaluru, Jamshedpur, and Dubai. With a remarkable track record in academics, state-of-the-art infrastructure, and significant contributions to research, MAHE has earned recognition and acclaim both nationally and internationally. In 2020, the Ministry of Education, Government of India, awarded MAHE the prestigious Institution of Eminence status. Currently ranked 3rd in the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) 2025 rankings, MAHE is the preferred choice for students seeking a transformative learning experience and enriching campus life, as well as for national and multinational corporations seeking top talent.
